spec.title: Ownership boundaries: VibeVM, Zap and PodBay

status.comment: Owner decision 2026-10-14; mandatory architecture and delegation contract.

p.VIBEVM-OWNER: VibeVM owns packages, their resolution/materialization/installation and workspace/context management: obtaining, assembling and managing the contextual data consumed by agents. Zap requests these through VibeVM contracts; it must not create another package resolver or context/workspace authority.

p.ZAP-OWNER: Zap is a long-horizon agent. It owns goals, plans, task semantics, priorities, task concurrency, adaptive replanning, logical work/attempt/result accounting and communication of task progress. It uses VibeVM data/context APIs and PodBay execution APIs. Model/effort choices and task-level economic policies belong here, not in the process operating system.

p.PODBAY-OWNER: PodBay is a cluster operating system for processes, including Zap and its workers. It owns placement, physical process identity/tree/relationships, launch, lifecycle, handles/references, sessions, I/O/output and supplied technical resource limits. It does not interpret goals, task completion/acceptance, package resolution or context assembly. Caller task/correlation identifiers may be carried opaquely without becoming process-layer task rules.

p.ZAP-RICH-PLANNING-LANGUAGE: VibeVM data/context contracts do not bound the expressiveness of Zap's planning language. During initial planning and replanning, Zap may and should expand owner-provided facts into richer goals, variables, conditions, constraints, alternatives, dependencies, estimates, hypotheses and predicted states. This is Zap-owned planning interpretation, not a second VibeVM package resolver or context-management authority.

p.SOURCE-VERSUS-PLAN: Derived planning models retain references to the VibeVM source/basis/version they interpret. Distinguish source facts from planning interpretations, assumptions, uncertainty and predictions; do not silently write derived planning truth back as VibeVM facts. Changed inputs may invalidate planning interpretations and trigger Zap replanning. A richer Zap language does not require equal schemas in the two projects.

implementation.title: 2. One authority and one process launch path

p.RUST-AUTHORITY: Production working logic is implemented in the Rust owner. JS/TS is thin presentation/transport and generated wire mirrors; moving a rule from TS into the wrong Rust project does not satisfy ownership. Reuse the owning project's existing API/records before proposing a missing contract. Boundary gaps are explicit owner-scoped work, not duplicate fallback engines.

p.MANAGED-PROCESS-PATH: Managed workers and other processes owned by Zap execute through PodBay. Zap must not retain a separate provider launcher, PTY manager or process tree. VibeVM supplies packages/context; Zap selects logical work; PodBay executes physical processes. Logical task dependencies and physical process relationships are distinct graphs with explicit links.

p.CONCURRENCY-BOUNDARY: Task concurrency/conflict/admission policy belongs to Zap. PodBay may enforce separately configured physical process/resource constraints and permission to create descendants. It must not use task states, priorities or acceptance to implement task concurrency. No cumulative lifetime child-launch quota is required or permitted as the default control; its removal must not be disguised as a task-planning policy in PodBay.

p.PACKET-OWNER-BLOCK: Every worker/reviewer packet includes this canonical anchor and an inline owner block: target project(s); rule/data/side-effect owner; exact neighboring APIs/data used; allowed changes; responsibilities that remain in the other projects. A quiet worker reads this named file and its bounded packet, not a full boot lane. This block applies to follow-ups and resumed workers as well as initial launch.

p.PACKET-OWNER-CHECK: The coordinator checks ownership before delegation and acceptance. A worker that needs an unnamed neighboring owner reports the exact boundary gap and obtains a corrected scope; it must not implement the neighbor's functionality locally. A cross-project task declares separate source/write owners and one integration owner. Reviews check both Rust-language placement and project ownership.

p.PACKET-INLINE-TEMPLATE: Owner block: VibeVM = packages/workspace/context. Zap = long-horizon goals/plans/task semantics/task concurrency, consuming VibeVM. PodBay = cluster process OS running Zap/workers, physical lifecycle/tree/resources/I/O. Target = named project. Neighbor use = named existing contract. Forbidden = duplicate neighboring authority. All working logic stays in the corresponding Rust owner; JS/TS stays thin.
